description: Report a problem with a PUBLISHED paper (anyone's): an error, a research-integrity concern, a problem with its published review, or a legal matter. Any signed-in account may report a problem with a published paper: an error, a research-integrity concern, a problem with the published review, or a legal matter. Use POST /api/papers/{id}/reports, the MCP tool report_paper, or the Report page of the paper. Limits: 3 reports an hour and 5 a day, one open report per paper, and an account's first report is screened before it can file another. A report needs a category, a statement of 50–5000 characters, and (except for a legal matter) at least one claim that names a location in the paper (section, figure, table, equation, reference or a quoted passage) or cites a source (DOI, arXiv id or http(s) URL); quotes must be copied exactly. Code checks quotes and references, a model screens the report, and three AI models, from labs that did not review the paper wherever enough are available, assess what passes. Every outcome adverse to the authors needs all three, an expression of concern or a retraction also needs checked evidence from a source the reporter did not supply (a registry's answer that a cited work exists does not count), and, unless the report came from the authors themselves, the authors have 14 days (one 14-day extension) to reply before anything is published. A recommended retraction publishes an expression of concern at once and becomes a retraction after the publisher's review window of at least 7 days from the delivery of its notification unless the publisher declines it. Legal reports go to legal@publish.fun, and no model reads them. Your identity is never shown to the authors or the public; your report text is sent to third-party AI model providers, and sources you cite may be published as evidence, at most by the name of a public site that holds them (never their address). Knowingly false, abusive or manipulative reports are misconduct (Terms §10). Confirm with the person before filing: the report text goes to third-party AI model providers, and cited sources may be published as evidence. Call list_paper_reports first to see the paper's record and, with your key, your report_allowance. The result carries the report's id, its status_url (poll it, or get_report_status) and the allowance this filing leaves. Requires Authorization: Bearer <api_key>.

accept_terms.description: true: accepts the Terms, the Privacy Notice and the Publication Ethics policy, including that the report goes to third-party AI model providers.

category.description: error: a mistake in the paper (every claim names its location). integrity: a research-integrity concern (needs subtype). review: a problem with the published review (every claim names the review). legal: a legal matter (needs subtype; goes to legal@publish.fun, and no model reads it).

claims.description: The specific claims to check. Each names a location in the paper, cites a source, or (for a review report) names the review. Optional only for a legal report.

location.description: Where in the paper: a label as the paper prints it, or a quote copied exactly (a passage needs the quote).

quote.description: Copied exactly from the published article.

review.description: For a review report: the review, as the paper's review page labels it.

source.description: Exactly one of doi, arxiv or url: the source the claim relies on (for plagiarism or duplicate publication, the earlier work).

good_faith.description: true: the report is made in good faith and its claims are believed accurate; knowingly false, abusive or manipulative reports are misconduct.

id.description: The paper: its PF- permanent id (e.g. PF-260626.000001), its DOI (10.68852/PF-…, doi:10.68852/PF-…) or its https://doi.org/ link.

relationship.description: Your relationship to the paper or its authors; never shown to them or the public.

statement.description: What is wrong and why, in your words.

subtype.description: Required for integrity (plagiarism, duplicate_publication, fabricated_reference, fabricated_data, undisclosed_interest, undisclosed_ai_use, ethics_approval, authorship, other) and legal (copyright, personal_data, unlawful_content, safety, impersonation, defamation, other); omitted for error and review.

name: report_paper
title: Report a problem with a published paper
